evidence.supportingExcerpt: Where the DNA sits was measured in different systems. In sequential muscle biopsies taken 3 and 12 months after an intramuscular AAV vector expressing alpha-1 antitrypsin, most vector DNA was double-stranded circular episomes, and clones recovered from the biopsies were transcriptionally active (Schnepp and colleagues; abstract read, full text not retrievable). After partial hepatectomy in mice, extrachromosomal genomes were the main form behind liver expression and in most cases no more than about 10 per cent of stably transduced genomes had integrated, although one of three mice at a higher dose had 67 per cent integrated genomes (Nakai and colleagues). That shows the usual behaviour of the tested vectors in those tissues, not that integration never happens, and persistent DNA does not show an intact cassette, enough protein or a surviving functional cell: in the muscle study the episomal inverted terminal repeats ranged from fully intact to severely deleted, so counting vector DNA is a different measurement from showing a working cassette.

Measure vector DNA with its cell or tissue denominator and distinguish genome integrity, DNA form, RNA, protein and function. An average DNA count does not identify an episome or an insertion site. A long-lived signal in one tissue does not establish survival, expression or genetic inheritance in a different dividing-cell population. Nonintegrated genomes can be diluted as cells divide. In Nakai's mouse liver-regeneration experiment, vector genomes per cell and factor IX expression fell after partial hepatectomy, whereas the integrated transposon comparator retained expression; this is a defined tissue/regeneration comparison.

proofs.requirement: The original and later packaging sentences are distinct: named viral-genome sizes and Wu's tested packaging result do not establish one universal payload limit.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Immunity and capacity also limit what a lot can do. In a phase 1/2 study in seven people with severe haemophilia B, an AAV2 factor IX vector infused through the hepatic artery reached therapeutic levels at the highest dose but expression lasted about 8 weeks; the authors' further studies suggested that cell-mediated immunity against capsid antigens destroyed transduced hepatocytes (Manno and colleagues). Neutralising antibodies against the capsid are why re-dosing is hard: a review notes that systemic AAV dosing needs patient stratification by antibody level and that re-administration then becomes very difficult (Naso and colleagues), and a 2024 mouse study, which opens by noting that AAV typically induces long-lasting neutralising antibodies that prevent re-administration, found that transient B-cell depletion (anti-CD20 with anti-BAFF) before hepatic AAV8 delivery allowed effective re-administration (Rana and colleagues). Whether a given product can be given again is a product-specific question, and that mouse experiment does not establish a clinical re-dosing protocol. For packaging, the AAV2 genome is a single-stranded DNA of 4,675 nucleotides (Srivastava and colleagues) and the original self-complementary-vector experiment used an inverted repeat that could pair with itself, bypassing synthesis of the second strand (McCarty and colleagues, 2001). McCarty's later review describes the trade-off as losing half the coding capacity. Report the capsid, cassette configuration and length being measured with a capacity figure; a measured packaged-genome length and usable coding capacity answer different questions. In the study of plasmid-encoded vectors of 4.7 to 8.7 kb in AAV2, AAV5 and AAV8 capsids, packaged genomes never exceeded 5.2 kb; genomes from plasmids over 5 kb were heterogeneous and truncated at the 5' end, and reporter expression in cells at high multiplicity of infection was substantially lower than from genomes under 5 kb (Wu and colleagues). FDA follow-up guidance says vectors such as AAV that do not tend to integrate or reactivate generally carry a lower risk of delayed adverse events, while product-specific modifications may change that, so safety is assessed per product.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A lentiviral vector is an engineered virus particle that delivers genetic instructions into cells, and in most designs those instructions are inserted into a chromosome. Getting in, being inserted, making protein and doing the intended job are four separate claims.

Three design labels are easy to confuse. Replication-defective means the delivered particle lacks the machinery to propagate as an ordinary virus, which does not replace testing: FDA guidance sets out testing of retroviral vector products, lentiviral ones included, for replication-competent virus during manufacture and in patient follow-up. Self-inactivating means regulatory sequences in the long terminal repeats are disabled: in the original design a 133 base-pair deletion in the U3 region of the 3' repeat was copied to the 5' repeat after reverse transcription and integration, and the vector still expressed from an internal promoter in rat brain and eye (Miyoshi and colleagues). It does not mean the cassette cannot integrate. Integration-deficient means integrase is mutated: with a class 1 integrase mutation, residual integration was lower than with intact integrase by a factor of 500 to 1,250, expression was transient in dividing cell lines and long-lived in non-dividing neural cultures and in mouse brain, consistent with an episomal genome (Philippe and colleagues). The name does not promise zero integration or lasting expression in dividing cells such as T cells.

proofs.requirement: A transposon cassette has recognition boundaries at both ends, with transposase as a separate component that recognises those ends.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A transposon system has two parts: a cargo cassette flanked by boundary sequences, and a transposase that recognises those boundaries and catalyses insertion. The transposase can be supplied as protein or through instructions that make it, and the cell has to receive both in usable form; the system does not itself deliver anything. Sleeping Beauty was reconstructed from inactive fish elements, and its transposase bound the inverted repeats and mediated precise cut-and-paste transposition in fish, mouse and human cells (Ivics and colleagues).

proofs.requirement: Chromosomal insertion requires its own copy-number and insertion-site evidence; a drawn position gives no equal-site probabilities.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Systems differ. In primary human T cells from peripheral blood and cord blood, piggyBac gave the highest stable gene transfer efficiency in the peripheral-blood cells and the most integrants in both, Tol2 and piggyBac were more likely to promote clonal expansion than Sleeping Beauty, and Tol2 and piggyBac integrated near transcription start sites and CpG islands while Sleeping Beauty integrations looked random (Huang and colleagues). That is a laboratory comparison, not a ranking of safety in patients. Insertion-site sequencing recovers only some junctions: in the Sleeping Beauty trial's 33 independent libraries most shared fewer than 20 per cent of sites with any other library, which the authors read as arguing against common hotspots, although some pairs shared over 40 per cent and 100,000 of 571,533 unique integrations were mapped. That describes those libraries, not every insertion or later clone, and an average copy number hides differences between cells. FDA follow-up guidance states that integration by transposon elements is not directed to specific sites and that continuing transposase in target cells creates the potential for remobilising an inserted element, so transposase persistence and cassette persistence are separate measurements.

An inserted cassette can be copied with chromosomal DNA during cell division; that genetic persistence does not guarantee continued expression, cell survival or useful activity. Report insertion sites, copy-number denominator, receptor-positive cells, retained transposase and antigen-dependent function separately. A mean copy count cannot recover the distribution across cells or all insertion sites.

proofs.requirement: Uptake into an endosomal compartment, cytosolic escape and protein expression are successive conditional outcomes, not synonyms.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A lipid nanoparticle is a formulated fat-based carrier that protects RNA and helps it enter cells. Getting into a cell, releasing usable RNA into the cell fluid and making protein are separate steps, and a particle can succeed at the first without the others.

A typical RNA-delivery lipid nanoparticle combines an ionisable lipid, a phospholipid, cholesterol and a polyethylene glycol lipid around the RNA; the proportions, lipid identities and preparation change behaviour, so the label LNP alone does not name a product. Ionisable lipids change charge with pH. In common designs they are more protonated in an acidic environment and less charged at physiological pH; the extent depends on the lipid and its environment. This can support membrane interactions during endosomal escape, whose performance remains formulation- and cell-dependent (Hou and colleagues, review). Cells usually take particles into endosomes, and messenger RNA is translated by ribosomes in the cytosol, so usable delivery needs the RNA to leave the endosome. Ordinary messenger RNA does not need to enter the nucleus.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In an invented comparison using 100 identified live cells per formulation at the same measurement time, A shows uptake in 70 cells and encoded protein in 10; B shows uptake in 40 and protein in 25. Uptake is therefore 70 versus 40 per cent, while protein expression is 10 versus 25 per cent on the same live-cell denominator. These separate counts do not show which cells had both signals, the fraction of intact RNA that escaped, the amount of protein per cell or a biological effect. Name the cargo, cell population, assay, timing and controls before comparing formulations; a brighter carrier signal alone does not establish usable RNA delivery.

proofs.requirement: Particle or fluorescent-lipid signal does not by itself establish intact RNA in the cytosol, encoded protein or useful function.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Where particles go depends on formulation and route. In female BALB/c mice given luciferase-mRNA LNPs by intramuscular, subcutaneous or intravenous injection, some intramuscular particles reached the liver and spleen, smaller particles more than larger ones, bigger particles tended to stay at the injection site, and liver expression was the most prominent; exposure and expression were not linearly related (Di and colleagues). Mouse distribution is not another product's distribution in people, and local injection does not establish local delivery. Readouts answer different questions: particle size, RNA integrity and encapsulated fraction describe the product; a labelled lipid or labelled RNA shows where a label went, not that intact RNA arrived or was released; and protein per identified live cell shows expression. In the mouse study a lipid label (DiR or deuterium-labelled cholesterol) and luciferase activity were measured separately and did not track each other linearly, and every figure needs its denominator (all cells, live cells or expressing cells). Uptake and protein are different fractions: in the six-formulation study the formulation with the highest eGFP expression had only moderate uptake, so a formulation that takes up in more cells can still make protein in fewer. Message and effect also run on separate clocks: in cultured mouse T cells CAR expression from LNP mRNA peaked at 24 hours and fell over the next days (Rurik and colleagues), and the same RNA in particles of different size or by a different route distributed differently, so the same RNA is not the same product.

proofs.requirement: Endosomal escape depends on formulation, cargo and studied cell context; named cell-model results are not one universal escape rate.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A typical RNA-delivery lipid nanoparticle combines an ionisable lipid, a phospholipid, cholesterol and a polyethylene glycol lipid around the RNA; the proportions, lipid identities and preparation change behaviour, so the label LNP alone does not name a product. Ionisable lipids change charge with pH. In common designs they are more protonated in an acidic environment and less charged at physiological pH; the extent depends on the lipid and its environment. This can support membrane interactions during endosomal escape, whose performance remains formulation- and cell-dependent (Hou and colleagues, review). Cells usually take particles into endosomes, and messenger RNA is translated by ribosomes in the cytosol, so usable delivery needs the RNA to leave the endosome. Ordinary messenger RNA does not need to enter the nucleus.

Uptake and expression were measured separately in primary human adipocytes, fibroblasts and HeLa cells with six LNP formulations of similar size (54 to 73 nm) carrying eGFP mRNA: total uptake was necessary but not a sufficient predictor of delivery, one formulation gave the highest eGFP expression despite moderate uptake, prolonged uptake impaired endosomal acidification and left mRNA in compartments unproductive for delivery, and early endocytic and recycling compartments had the highest probability of escape (Paramasivam and colleagues). In that study eGFP expression served as a proxy for release; it did not measure the fraction of RNA that escaped.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Where particles go depends on formulation and route. In female BALB/c mice given luciferase-mRNA LNPs by intramuscular, subcutaneous or intravenous injection, some intramuscular particles reached the liver and spleen, smaller particles more than larger ones, bigger particles tended to stay at the injection site, and liver expression was the most prominent; exposure and expression were not linearly related (Di and colleagues). Mouse distribution is not another product's distribution in people, and local injection does not establish local delivery. Readouts answer different questions: particle size, RNA integrity and encapsulated fraction describe the product; a labelled lipid or labelled RNA shows where a label went, not that intact RNA arrived or was released; and protein per identified live cell shows expression. In the mouse study a lipid label (DiR or deuterium-labelled cholesterol) and luciferase activity were measured separately and did not track each other linearly, and every figure needs its denominator (all cells, live cells or expressing cells). Uptake and protein are different fractions: in the six-formulation study the formulation with the highest eGFP expression had only moderate uptake, so a formulation that takes up in more cells can still make protein in fewer. The cancer relevance is as a carrier of antigen-encoding RNA or of instructions for engineering immune cells. The carrier, where it goes, which cells make protein and what that protein does are different questions; none of these studies is evidence of clinical benefit.
